items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had Elvin Jones, Tommy Flanagan, Jimmy Forest, and Tommy Potter. I had that band for about four or five years.

ctx.x: I guess it was about ’65, because my daughter was born in 1965. It was about 1962, ’63, something like that. I had a band…’55, ’56, ’57, ’58, I had Elvin Jones, Tommy Flanagan, Jimmy Forest, and Tommy Potter. I had that band for about four or five years.
Were you based in New York with that band?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: I got Tommy Potter and Tommy Flanagan and Elvin Jones... And then Roland Hanna, he came in after Tommy Flanagan and played with me.

ctx.x: Oh, yes, you almost wanted to --

Yeah, wanted to go to New York, anyway. So I think my first was Jimmy Forrest, Joe Benjamin and Jimmy Jones was on piano, and oh, what's the drummer's name in New York, not Elvin because Elvin came latter. He played with Billy Eckstine for a long time. Good drummer.* Anyway, they opened up with me. And it was a fantastic night, you know.
And Joe Benjamin, after he left, then I got Tommy Potter and Tommy Flanagan and Elvin Jones.
